comparisons.peer_summary: Competition for skilled executives and employees in AI and machine learning is intense, and failure to attract, train, and retain key personnel could hinder product development, affected by stock-based compensation value and future restructuring plans.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD disclose significant risks regarding the recruitment and retention of engineering and technical personnel, emphasizing that stock-based compensation is a critical tool that is sensitive to stock price performance. AVGO specifically notes the impact of stock underperformance on retention efforts, stating, 'If we are unable to continue our current equity granting philosophy or our stock underperforms, this could impair our efforts to attract and retain necessary personnel' (avgo_2024_1A_P029_S006). Similarly, AMD highlights that if stock awards do not appreciate or are viewed as less valuable, 'our ability to attract, retain and motivate our executives and employees could be weakened' (amd_2024_1A_P140_S005). Both companies also explicitly identify engineers as central to their innovation and strategy, with AMD stating, 'Much of our future success depends upon the continued service of numerous qualified engineering, marketing, sales and executive employees' (amd_2024_1A_P140_S001).

sentences.text: If we are unable to continue our current equity granting philosophy or our stock underperforms, this could impair our efforts to attract and retain necessary personnel.
If we are unable to attract and retain qualified personnel, especially our engineering and technical personnel, we may not be able to execute our business strategy effectively.

If the value of such stock awards does not appreciate as measured by the performance of the price of our common stock, or if our share-based compensation otherwise ceases to be viewed as a valuable benefit, our ability to attract, retain and motivate our executives and employees could be weakened, which could harm our results of operations.
Much of our future success depends upon the continued service of numerous qualified engineering, marketing, sales and executive employees.

comparisons.peer_topic: Human Capital Challenges and Workforce Turnover
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel faces intense competition for technical talent, which is exacerbated by remote work flexibility and immigration policies. High turnover and restructuring efforts, including headcount reductions in 2022 and 2024, along with reduced retention value of share-based awards due to stock price declines, can harm operations and recruitment.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and INTC both cite immigration laws as a specific factor limiting the pool of available engineering talent. AVGO reports that 'current or future immigration laws may make it more difficult to hire or retain qualified engineers, further limiting the pool of available talent' (avgo_2024_1A_P029_S004). INTC similarly warns that 'changes in immigration policies may further limit the pool of available talent and impair our ability to recruit and hire technical and professional talent' (intc_2024_1A_P070_S004). Additionally, both firms utilize share-based awards to mitigate retention risks; AVGO notes its reliance on equity granting philosophy (avgo_2024_1A_P029_S006), while INTC states, 'To help attract, retain, and motivate qualified employees, we use share-based awards, such as RSUs' (intc_2024_1A_P070_S008).

sentences.text: In addition, current or future immigration laws may make it more difficult to hire or retain qualified engineers, further limiting the pool of available talent.
If we are unable to continue our current equity granting philosophy or our stock underperforms, this could impair our efforts to attract and retain necessary personnel.
In addition, changes in immigration policies may further limit the pool of available talent and impair our ability to recruit and hire technical and professional talent.
To help attract, retain, and motivate qualified employees, we use share-based awards, such as RSUs, and performance-based cash incentive awards.

comparisons.peer_topic: Human Capital and Talent Retention Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: The company must attract and retain highly skilled employees to remain competitive; high attrition, intense competition for talent, and immigration policy changes may increase costs or disrupt operations.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and MU identify immigration policy changes as a risk to retaining technical talent. AVGO discloses that 'immigration laws may make it more difficult to hire or retain qualified engineers' (avgo_2024_1A_P029_S004), while MU states that 'changes to immigration policies... may limit our ability to hire and/or retain talent' (mu_2024_1A_P079_S003). Both companies also frame the ability to attract and retain skilled personnel as critical to executing business strategy, with AVGO noting that failure to do so means 'we may not be able to execute our business strategy effectively' (avgo_2024_1A_P028_S001) and MU warning that inability to retain talent 'could inhibit our ability to maintain or expand our business operations' (mu_2024_1A_P080_S002).

sentences.text: In addition, current or future immigration laws may make it more difficult to hire or retain qualified engineers, further limiting the pool of available talent.
If we are unable to attract and retain qualified personnel, especially our engineering and technical personnel, we may not be able to execute our business strategy effectively.

Additionally, changes to immigration policies in the countries in which we operate, as well as restrictions on travel due to public health crises or other causes, may limit our ability to hire and/or retain talent in, or transfer talent to, specific locations.
Our inability to do so could inhibit our ability to maintain or expand our business operations and may adversely impact our operating results.

comparisons.peer_topic: Executive Retention and Key Personnel Dependency
comparisons.peer_summary: The business is highly dependent on the longstanding executive team, and failure to attract, retain, and motivate executives and key employees, or to ensure effective succession planning, could harm the business. Labor market competition and immigration regulations also impact this ability.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and NVDA share specific disclosures on how stock price volatility impacts the retention value of equity awards. AVGO states, 'If we are unable to continue our current equity granting philosophy or our stock underperforms, this could impair our efforts to attract and retain necessary personnel' (avgo_2024_1A_P029_S006). NVDA explicitly links stock volatility to decreased retentive value, noting that 'in times of stock price volatility... the retentive value of our stock-based compensation may decrease' (nvda_2024_1A_P059_S004). Both companies also flag immigration regulations as a barrier to hiring qualified employees, with AVGO citing 'current or future immigration laws' (avgo_2024_1A_P029_S004) and NVDA warning that 'Changes in immigration and work permit regulations... could impair our ability to attract and retain qualified employees' (nvda_2024_1A_P059_S003).

sentences.text: If we are unable to continue our current equity granting philosophy or our stock underperforms, this could impair our efforts to attract and retain necessary personnel.
In addition, current or future immigration laws may make it more difficult to hire or retain qualified engineers, further limiting the pool of available talent.

Competition for personnel results in increased costs in the form of cash and stock-based compensation, and in times of stock price volatility, as we have experienced in the past and may experience in the future, the retentive value of our stock-based compensation may decrease.
Changes in immigration and work permit regulations or in their administration or interpretation could impair our ability to attract and retain qualified employees.

comparisons.peer_topic: Human Capital Retention and Recruitment Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: The company faces intense competition for specialized engineering talent and key management, exacerbated by remote work options, larger competitors with superior compensation or benefits, and restrictive immigration laws for foreign national graduates.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and QCOM both highlight the constraining effect of immigration laws on the available talent pool for technical roles. AVGO discloses that 'current or future immigration laws may make it more difficult to hire or retain qualified engineers, further limiting the pool of available talent' (avgo_2024_1A_P029_S004). QCOM provides a similar assessment, stating that 'existing immigration laws make it more difficult for us to recruit and retain highly skilled foreign national graduates... making the pool of available talent even smaller' (qcom_2024_1A_P061_S007). Both companies also recognize the critical nature of technical personnel for business execution, with AVGO noting the inability to attract/retain personnel hinders 'execute our business strategy effectively' (avgo_2024_1A_P028_S001) and QCOM stating success depends on the ability to 'attract, retain and motivate' technical personnel who drive 'technological and product innovations' (qcom_2024_1A_P061_S002).

sentences.text: In addition, current or future immigration laws may make it more difficult to hire or retain qualified engineers, further limiting the pool of available talent.
If we are unable to attract and retain qualified personnel, especially our engineering and technical personnel, we may not be able to execute our business strategy effectively.

Further, existing immigration laws make it more difficult for us to recruit and retain highly skilled foreign national graduates of universities in the United States, making the pool of available talent even smaller.
Implementing our business strategy requires specialized engineering and other talent, as our revenues are highly dependent on technological and product innovations.
